title: feat(emulate): add Windows Chrome 156 profile
body:
Adds a Windows Chrome 156 profile with the version-seeded Client Hints brand order, a navigation Accept header including image/jxl, sorted trust anchors, and an explicit zero-byte server-padding request.

Depends on https://github.com/0x676e67/wreq/pull/1362. The wreq git patch temporarily points to that PR head so this branch can compile before its API is released; it must be updated to the accepted upstream revision before merging.

The profile targets the initial TLS/HTTP2 configuration observed with Windows Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.73. Server padding is experimental and configuration-dependent. Chrome for Testing uses Chromium branding; the Google Chrome brand list is derived from Chromium's version-seeded ordering. Other platforms, resumed sessions, HTTP3, and complete browser equivalence are not validated.

Extends the trust-anchor checks and adds loopback ClientHello tests for extension 4832 (payload 0000), covering client-wide/per-request emulation and fresh connections. The Chrome154 control omits that extension. Existing profiles are unchanged.

Formatting and diff checks pass. An equivalent native consumer profile has compiled and emitted the expected extension. Repository Cargo tests are delegated to CI because the available local Rust 1.94.1 is below the required 1.98.

title: feat(tower): add client hints middleware
body:
Adds `ClientHintsLayer` under a new `tower-client-hints` feature, for 0x676e67/wreq#1299.

The layer remembers which hints each origin asked for in `Accept-CH` and sends them on later requests. If a response has `Critical-CH` with an accepted hint the request didn't have, it sends the request once more with the hints. Same as Chrome, only `GET` and `HEAD` get resent.

Hint values come from `Hints::from_emulation`, which handles the Chrome profiles on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android and returns `None` for everything else. Full version is taken from the User-Agent if it isn't reduced, otherwise from a table of the last stable build for each milestone (100 to 154) that I pulled from Google's VersionHistory API.

I compared it with headless Chrome 154 against a local server: when it restarts, which hints go out, header order, and that a `POST` isn't resent. On www.indeed.com Chrome131 and Chrome136 now get a 302 instead of a 403. Chrome120 and Chrome142 still get a 403 after the retry, and most other profiles aren't challenged anymore, so it hits fewer profiles than when I opened the issue.

I also measured the overhead (before the per-hop change). Against a local HTTP/1 server the worst case (every response sends `Accept-CH`) goes from about 29 to 32 µs per request, so around 3 µs and ~40 extra allocations. If the origin never sends `Accept-CH` it's about 0.35 µs. A real request to a remote server takes milliseconds, so it doesn't really matter there.

Redirects use the per-hop callbacks from 0x676e67/wreq#1345 (the git patch points at its head). `client_hints::redirect(Policy::default())` sets them on the client: each hop gets the hints its own origin accepts, `Accept-CH` from every redirect is remembered as it arrives, and a redirect with `Critical-CH` for a missing hint stops and restarts the request from its first URL. I compared it with headless Chrome 155 on cross-origin redirects, `Accept-CH` on a redirect and `Critical-CH` on a redirect, and it sends the same hints on every request. Without the callbacks it works like before, the hints picked for the first origin stay on every hop.

Added `--features tower-client-hints` to the nextest step so the new tests actually run in CI. The origin store uses `lru`, which wreq already pulls in. Clippy is clean with `--all-targets --all-features`.

I tried to follow the existing patterns as close as I could (the delay middleware and the layers in wreq), but some things may still need adjusting to the codebase's style, happy to change them.

Closes 0x676e67/wreq#1299
